chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Does the menstruating woman make up the Prayer?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'Does she make up the Fast?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'From where does that come?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the first one who analogized was Iblis'. I said, 'And the fasting one can submerge in the water?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'So can he wear wet clothes upon his body?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'From where does that come?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'From that'. I said, 'Does the fasting one smell the rosemary?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, because it is a pleasure, and it is disliked for him to derive pleasure.'

key_terms.تَقْضِي: She makes up (missed acts of worship)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a menstruating woman regarding making up prayers and fasting, and what is disliked for a fasting person regarding scents?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the asymmetry in religious obligations, noting that while menstruating women are exempt from prayer, they must make up fasting, a distinction rooted in the concept of 'Qias' (analogical reasoning) attributed to Iblis. It further details specific rulings for the fasting individual, permitting submersion in water but prohibiting deriving pleasure from scents like rosemary, as the essence of fasting is the restraint of sensory enjoyment.
